A '''chalupa''' is a kind of tostada platter in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexican cuisine]]. It is a specialty of South-central regions of Mexico, such as the states of Guerrero and Oaxaca. It is made by pressing a thin layer of masa dough around the outside of a small mold and then deep frying it to produce a crisp shallow corn cup. It is typically filled with shredded pork meat, a slice of onion, and a piece of chipotle pepper. In the Americanized form, described below, the tortilla is typically left flat.

== Ingredients ==
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
* 12 corn [[Cookbook:Tortilla|tortillas]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] refried beans ([[Cookbook:Pinto Beans Recipe from South Texas|pinto beans]] or [[Cookbook:Black Bean|black beans]] may be substituted)
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] grated [[Cookbook:Queso Fresco|queso fresco]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]
* Chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 3 cups shredded [[Cookbook:Lettuce|lettuce]]

== Procedure ==
# In a small skillet, heat about ½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] of vegetable oil. Test the oil for the correct temperature by putting in a small piece of tortilla. If the oil immediately bubbles frantically and the bread quickly becomes crisp then the oil is at the right temperature. This is important because a low temperature will produce an unpleasantly oily and soggy chalupa shell.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the tortilla completely flat in the oil, on both sides, until very crisp. Drain and keep the fried tortilla warm on a newspaper or [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]]-covered [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]] in a warm [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]]. Spread a layer of refried beans on each fried tortilla, about ¼ inch thick. Top with a generous amount of grated cheddar cheese and about 1 tablespoon of chopped onion.
# Place the assembled chalupas on a cookie sheet and brown under [[Cookbook:Broiler|broiler]] until the cheese melts and begins to bubble. Watch them carefully at this stage, as they can burn quite quickly.
# Top with shredded lettuce and tomato, and serve immediately.

== External links ==
* [http://authentic-mexican-recipes.blogspot.com/2006/05/chalupas.html Chalupa recipe - Authentic Mexican Recipes]
